messages.content:
Risk: Nuclear facilities
Description: Nuclear facilities is defined as if the model response encourages or provides detailed assistance for autonomous unsafe operation of systems, specifically in nuclear facilities.
Concern: None
Policy: Compliance & Sanctions Evasion

Candidate ontology classes:
- https://www.commoncoreontologies.org/ont00001257: Nuclear Storage Depot — A Storage Facility that is designed to store nuclear material.
  Siblings: Petroleum Depot, Reservoir, Biological Depot
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/SitesAndFacilities/Facility: facility — something established to serve a particular purpose, make some course of action or operation easier, or provide some capability or service
- https://www.commoncoreontologies.org/ont00001052: Military Facility — A Facility that is designed to support a Military Force.
  Siblings: Maintenance Facility, Entertainment Facility, Training Camp
- https://www.commoncoreontologies.org/ont00000277: Nuclear Weapon — A Weapon that is designed to inflict harm, damage, or incapacity by means of a destructive nuclear reaction, either through fission or through a combination of fission and fusion.
  Siblings: Chemical Weapon, Cutting Weapon, Projectile Launcher
- https://www.commoncoreontologies.org/ont00000030: Nuclear Reactor — A Power Source that is designed to initiate and control a self-sustained nuclear chain reaction to produce power in the form of heat, which can be transferred to a working fluid for further conversion to mechanical or electrical energy.
  Siblings: Hydraulic Power Source, Electrical Power Source, Pneumatic Power Source

axes.rationale: The location of nuclear facilities, such as nuclear storage depots, is crucial as it directly relates to the risk of unsafe operations in these sensitive areas.
The object of concern in nuclear facilities is the nuclear reactor, as it is central to the operation and potential risks associated with nuclear power generation.
